title: Listening to Johnny Dodds at Naulties Hall
summary: As a boy Harry sat outside Naulties Hall to hear Johnny Dodds and Joe Oliver, and liked other clarinetists, around World War I.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, I think you told me once you'd maybe heard Johnny Dodds, was it? Or?

Oh, I used to listen to Johnny Dodds a lot. Did he live near you? I don't know where he lived, but he used to play at Naulties Hall and Josephine between Magnolia and South Robinson. That wasn't too far from where I lived. Oh, definitely. And of course, I studied in the clarinet, you know, and I was interested and naturally I'd just go down there and sit across the street on the step all night long and listen to him. Listen. Or wherever there was a band.
I'd get there and listen, you know. And especially if it was a clarinet play, I liked Mike. And I liked Johnny Dodds.
How old were you then? Of course, I never heard him in the old days. I heard him right before he died in Chicago and in some of his records. And I don't know how he played pretty well.
I thought he played very good. He worked with Joe Oliver. Joe Oliver. Uh-huh. I think they played there two or three nights a week at Naulties Hall.
But how old would you have been then? You'd already taken up the clarinet then.
Oh, I'd say that was during World War I.
Maybe a little before. Yeah. Maybe a little after. I don't remember, but I was quite young.
